instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the upper third. Line a large sheet pan with parchment.
In a small dish, mix the 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.

Pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and lay it on the pan with space between the fillets. Sprinkle the spice mix evenly over both sides. Drizzle the 1 tbsp olive oil over the top and dot each fillet with a little of the 1 tbsp butter.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily when you press it with a fork.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Squeeze one of the limes, about 2 tbsp of juice, into a medium bowl. Add the 1/2 cup sour cream, the 1/3 cup mayonnaise and the 1 tsp garlic powder and whisk until it's smooth.

Shred half the cabbage very thin and put it in a bowl. Finely dice half the onion and chop a small handful of the cilantro, and add both to the cabbage. Squeeze half of the other lime over it, add a pinch of salt and toss. Cut the last lime half into wedges.
Slice the 2 avocados and grate the cotija.
When the fish is done, turn the oven to broil. Broil the fish for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges are golden and crisp. Watch it closely. It goes from golden to burnt fast.

While the fish broils, heat a large dry skillet over medium high. Warm the 12 tortillas one or two at a time for about 30 seconds, then flip them and warm the other side until they're soft and have a few brown spots. Stack them in a clean kitchen towel and wrap them up.
Break the fish into large flakes with a fork. Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Serve the fish with the warm tortillas, the slaw, avocado, cotija, sauce and lime wedges, with the sriracha on the side.
method_notes: All three put white fish in warm corn tortillas with shredded cabbage, red onion, cilantro and a creamy lime sauce. Natasha's Kitchen, the lead, rubs tilapia with cumin, cayenne, salt and pepper, bakes it with olive oil and butter, broils it to brown the edges, and makes the sauce from sour cream, mayonnaise, lime, garlic powder and a little sriracha. Salt and Lavender marinates cod in chili powder and lime and pan fries it in butter, and Tasty fries beer-battered cod and dresses its slaw with lime and salt. This one follows the lead, swaps the cayenne for smoked paprika so the base stays mild with sriracha at the table, and tosses the cabbage with lime the way Tasty does.
